intro: Lesson 21: The Farewell Sermon: women, equality and holding to the Qur'an. To understand the sermon's teaching on women's rights, equality and holding to the Qur'an

passage.title: Qur'an, al-Hujurat 49:13 (translation of the meaning)
paras: O mankind, We created you from a male and a female and made you peoples and tribes that you may know one another. Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you.

questions.q: Explain what the sermon and 49:13 teach about racism.
questions.a: No one is better by race; Allah made peoples to know one another; honour is by taqwa.
questions.model: Point: Islam rejects racism. Evidence: 49:13: 'the most noble of you ... is the most righteous'. Explain: colour and tribe are for knowing each other, not ranking. Link: the sermon taught this to over a hundred thousand people of many tribes.

questions.q: 'Let the one present inform the absent' is in ...
In the portal response box, write a 12-mark style practice: 'The Farewell Sermon is still relevant today.' Give two reasons for, one against, and a conclusion. Start: 'Some would agree because ...'
questions.a: For: equality (49:13), sanctity of life, women's rights, holding to the Qur'an; against: some issues (e.g. blood feuds) belong to that time; conclusion with justification
questions.model: Teacher writes the first 'for' paragraph opening: 'Some would agree because the sermon's teaching on equality answers racism today: 49:13 says ...'

questions.q: what is your duty from 'let the one present inform the absent'?
questions.a: To pass on what we learn of Islam accurately.

questions.q: how did early Muslims carry out this command?
questions.a: They taught others, recorded hadith and spread to new lands.

questions.q: Equality in Islam is measured by ...
Back to our ponder: what does Islam say about being 'better'?
questions.a: Only taqwa raises a person with Allah (49:13).
